reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. The port pipeline is fast once something appears (conditional P ~0.8), but the unconditional chance of a SCORED probe by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC is ~0.2-0.25, far below the 0.7 bar. Four parts of the plan also cannot run as written. (1) Unconditional probability (GUESSES): P(a public notebook >= 0.954 appears, and we see it, by ~29 Sep 00:00 UTC) ~0.25-0.3. That is the idea's own 0.3; the sibling value verdict gives 0.2-0.3, since both authors publish BELOW their own scores: Tennant's newest public kernel is 0.946 against his 0.959, and Pothula released 0.953 at 0.956. Times P(all its datasets are public and attachable) ~0.85. Times P(the verbatim copy runs and submits in time) ~0.9. Result: ~0.2. (2) This container cannot pull or push: I checked, and www.kaggle.com/api/v1 gets CONNECT 403 from the proxy. So the 'agent-container 2 h' resource line is wrong: pull, push and the dummy run must go through the laptop agent that holds kaggle.json (CONTEXT.md l.39, l.613), with git as the handoff. For the same reason, the user's offer to paste the Kaggle API key into this chat would not help here, and a secret should not be pasted anyway. (3) 'build_probe_kernel --base <successor>' does not exist. --base takes only {exp39, x138}. BASES hard-codes a sha256 and cell indices (x138: config 2, predict 4, post 5), and allows only divinsert/leafprune. Every patch uses _rep1, which asserts that its anchor occurs exactly once. The step-(3) rider on a successor therefore means a new BASES entry plus anchor repair, about 1-3 h. If the successor edits the post cell near the divinsert anchors, add a second dummy run (0.7 GPU-h). The VERBATIM copy needs none of this: copy the ipynb and kernel-metadata.json, which carries the docker_image pin and machine_shape as in exp56, change the id, then push. (4) The watch is too sparse and in the wrong place. There are only three browser sweeps, at 06:00 UTC on 26, 27 and 28 Sep. A release after 28 Sep 06:00 would be missed, yet with 7-10 h latency (CONTEXT l.1525) a release seen by 29 Sep ~07:00 can still be submitted by 10:00 and inform the finals. Late releases are also the most likely kind. The laptop's Kaggle CLI can poll kernel lists and the leaderboard without the user's browser. The cited numbers check out: Tennant r32 0.959 and Pothula r58 0.956 (pass2 l.110-111); 41 teams at 0.953 (pass2 l.107); the stub notebook dated 24 Sep, which is empty (pass2 l.18); x138 = readmit-v1 + head (DIFF.md s.1). The runtime is not a problem: the author's own scored run proves it fits 12 h on Kaggle's scorer, and x138's REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 27000 guard covers slow movies. GPU is not a constraint either: 0.7 GPU-h per dummy run out of 30 after the 26 Sep 00:00 reset. LB slots are not a constraint: at most 1-2 of the 21 slots. A WebSearch today found no new author notebook indexed.
fix_if_any: Keep it as a ZERO-COST TRIGGERED WATCH, not a planned line, and change the mechanics. (a) Discovery goes to the laptop agent (kaggle.json), polling every ~4 h from 26 Sep 00:00 to 29 Sep 07:00 UTC with: `kaggle kernels list --competition biohub-cell-tracking-during-development --sort-by scoreDescending -p 1`; `kaggle kernels list --user thtennant --sort-by dateRun`; the same for --user anvithpothula; and `kaggle competitions leaderboard biohub-cell-tracking-during-development -s`, looking for a new spike of >= 10 teams at one score >= 0.955. The user's browser does one sweep a day as a backup (title inflation check, comments). (b) Pre-checks on the trigger, 15 min: public score >= 0.956 (the value verdict's bar; 0.954 is inside noise). Every dataset_source and model_source public (`kaggle datasets metadata`); if any is private, abort and at most leave a comment. No internet. (c) VERBATIM PATH, no builder change: `kaggle kernels pull <id> -m` -> experiments/expNN_<slug>_verbatim; change only the id and title in kernel-metadata.json and keep docker_image and machine_shape; push; dummy run 15-40 min; gate = no REPAIR FAILED and node/edge counts on the 4 clips within 1% of the author's log; user OK; submit. About 1.5 h from trigger to submission. Do the cell-by-cell diff against exp56 in parallel (container, via git), not on the critical path. (d) RIDER PATH, only after the verbatim copy has scored and only if #35 > #34: add a BASES entry in tools/build_probe_kernel.py (new sha256 and cell indices), run the divinsert anchors, and require a byte-identical no-op build with DIVINS_ENABLE=0. About 1-3 h plus 0.7 GPU-h. (e) Hard cut-offs: verbatim submitted by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC, so trigger by ~08:00. Rider only if the verbatim copy is scored by 28 Sep 22:00 UTC. (f) Reserve nothing in advance: 1.5 GPU-h and 2 LB slots come out of the pool only when a trigger fires. Framed this way the watch costs ~0.3 agent-h a day. It does not meet the 70% bar unconditionally, and nothing can make publication by a third party likely, so the final plan must not depend on it.
